context:
Goal: the shared-tree guard stops destructive git that Claude runs by mistake.
Problem (risk): a Python heredoc with os.system("git reset --hard ...") or subprocess.run(["git","reset","--hard"]) passes the guard. The bash forms are refused.
Based on (code): hooks/guard_shared_tree.py reads no Python body (probed on main 174b005c1).
Based on (ruling): decision guard-guards-mistakes-only: a guard stops forms Claude could write by mistake. Asked because whether Claude runs git through Python by mistake is a judgment call.
Departs from: main reads no Python body for git discards. Option a adds that read.

lastAnswer.note: i feel like maybe we went down this way and then reverted? is that true or no

options.label: Read git discard calls in Python heredoc strings
options.lose: False alarms on Python text that only mentions those commands.

options.label: Keep the gap; Claude rarely runs git through Python (recommended)

reply: Lane notes-keep-reverify, 14:48 CST, on "did we go down this way and then revert?": no. Nothing was built and reverted. From the guard's start (739412841, 2026-09-16) a test pinned this as a known hole: git stash inside a Python string was allowed. Commit 8ef6956b4 (2026-10-15) removed only that test case. The guard has never read Python bodies for git discards. Pick a or b.
short: Shared-tree guard: read git reset inside Python, or keep the gap
title: Should the shared-tree guard read git discards inside Python code?
why: Lane notes-keep-reverify, from kept note guard-heredoc-os-system.
